REQUIREMENTS_ANALYSIS.EFFECTIVE_SPECIFICATION: Only ISSUE32 defines the target contract. Previous specifications are available in immutable Git history and Issue #25 approval discussions; they are not part of these active XML artifacts. No /v1, /v2, Bearer, legacy-client support or data migration.

ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.SCOPE: Target-only correction. Historical approved clauses and approval records remain as evidence of prior decisions; incompatible historical API paths are not the target contract. No production implementation authorized.
ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.GOAL: One unified direct/group conversation service exposed solely through the unversioned /conversations HTTP resource tree, authenticated exclusively with BFE Drive Internal Auth validated DPoP-bound sessions.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All target conversation HTTP operations use /conversations and its unversioned descendants. /v1 and /v2 are not target HTTP APIs. Existing /v2 domain behavior is the implementation migration baseline, not a second API.

Every protected target HTTP request requires DPoP proof bound to the validated BFE Drive session through existing Internal Auth; plain Bearer is not an accepted authentication scheme. WebSocket authentication and subscriptions preserve required independent membership verification and revocation rules.
Direct and group conversations share one conversation identity, message stream, authorization model and history semantics, retaining type-specific membership and ownership rules.

Retain all functional direct/group conversation behavior, permissions, message/document handling and idempotency from the working /v2 implementation. No legacy-client support, production-data inventory or migration is in scope; destructive removal of populated legacy tables is not authorized.

A 1:1 conversation is created by authenticated account UUID and distinct peer UUID. Self-direct is rejected. Creation for the same unordered pair is unique and concurrency-safe. Personal hide affects only caller visibility, never peer access, messages or direct identity.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for direct without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Authenticated user creates named group with owner and selected account UUIDs. Maximum 100 members including owner. Creator is owner. Group supports rename, invited-member changes, role management and departure. A member may leave. The owner must transfer ownership to another current group member before leaving; if there is no other current member, the last owner cannot leave. Exactly one owner must remain after each successful operation.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for group without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Owner may manage group and appoint or dismiss admins, while preserving exactly one owner; admin can only perform explicitly allowed membership or rename operations, cannot remove owner/other admin, appoint admins or transfer ownership; member cannot administer group. BFE Drive ADMIN status does not grant Chat membership or management.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for roles without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Every membership addition/removal creates an auditable bounded visibility interval. Read and message delivery are permitted only for messages within caller intervals. On rejoin, messages from the gap stay hidden. Removal immediately blocks subsequent protected operations and active WebSocket subscriptions. Membership mutations and send/delivery authorization have a defined atomic ordering.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for membership without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Each conversation has one stable monotonic conversation-scoped message order and cursor pagination, default 50 and max 100 messages per page. Every history query filters by authenticated viewer membership intervals. The same visibility rule applies to reconnect and historical catch-up.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for history without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Only authenticated current members send messages; sender identity is never supplied by a trusted client field. Text maximum 16384 UTF-8 bytes, request JSON maximum 65536 bytes. Idempotency key replay returns original result for identical content and 409 Conflict for different content; concurrency cannot create duplicates.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for message without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Optional message context holds document ID and title; preserve both in message history and events. Chat neither copies document content nor grants any BFE Drive document rights. Document access is independently checked by BFE Drive.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for document without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Centrifuge publishes persisted messages only to currently authorized members. Revalidate authorized subscriptions and revocation even for established sockets. Reconnect recovers missed messages through persisted conversation history; multi-device membership and read states remain coherent.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for realtime without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Read marker is monotonically increasing per account and conversation and shared across devices. Unread counts include only authorized messages sent by other users. One member cannot advance another member read marker.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for read without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All Chat-specific conversation state and ACLs are within bfe_chat. BFE Drive sessions are validated through existing Internal Auth UDS; account UUID alone grants no Chat authorization. Reject out-of-scope access without leaking data.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for isolation without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Group names limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes; no more than 100 group members; JSON body max 65536 bytes; message text max 16384 UTF-8 bytes; history page max 100. Reject invalid input before changes or publications.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for limits without changes to legacy clients or production data.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.SCOPE: Requirements-only change confined to bogachenko/bfe-chat-service. Propose replacing Centrifuge with ntfy as the sole chat realtime notification transport within this service. The proposal is not effective until Human Approval; the approved ISSUE32 baseline remains effective. This revision authorizes no implementation, dependency change, production configuration change, database operation, merge to the effective baseline, or deployment. It does not authorize changes to BFE Drive, other repositories, client applications, or external infrastructure. Preserve the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth/DPoP integration and the approved Chat HTTP authentication contract.
ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.PROJECT_GOAL: Replace Centrifuge with ntfy for realtime wake-up notifications while preserving backend-authoritative history, authorization, membership visibility, sender exclusion, document privacy, and production safeguards.

PROPOSED_ACCEPTANCE_LIMITS.LIMIT: Maximum interval from authoritative session or membership revocation to termination of every active subscription and cessation of protected event delivery.
PROPOSED_ACCEPTANCE_LIMITS.NOTE: The revocation bound is a proposed service-side value for Project Owner approval, not an effective production guarantee. Technology must prove that it can be met without changing the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth contract. If rejected or infeasible, revise the requirement before Human Approval; implementation may not choose a substitute silently.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.ACTOR: Authenticated current conversation member other than the sender

USE_CASE.ACTION: Commits a chat message through the backend
USE_CASE.GOAL: Notify other currently authorized members that backend history may have changed without disclosing message or document data through ntfy

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy replaces Centrifuge as the sole target chat realtime notification transport. The target must not retain Centrifuge as a parallel or fallback realtime transport. ntfy is only a wake-up/invalidation channel; PostgreSQL-backed backend state and authorized HTTP history remain the source of truth for messages, order, membership, and visibility.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: The approved target architecture and later runtime/dependency inventory identify ntfy as the only realtime notification transport and show no Centrifuge runtime path. A notification alone cannot return or authorize access to message data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The backend is the only authority for recipient selection, topic provisioning, publishing, and subscription authorization. Every protected Chat HTTP request preserves the approved BFE Drive Internal Auth/DPoP contract: the service validates the current session through the existing Internal Auth UDS integration, validates the DPoP proof including signature, method/target binding, access-token hash and replay protection, and derives the account identity from the validated result. The existing HTTP contract continues to require the DPoP authorization scheme and proof header; Bearer-only authentication remains rejected. Before granting ntfy topic access to a connecting caller, the service validates that caller's current session through this existing mechanism and checks current conversation membership and epoch. Before publishing a notification, the service validates the sender through the existing authenticated HTTP request and checks recipient membership and epoch in backend state; it must not assume it can validate another user's BFE session without that user's credentials. If active ntfy access must be revoked on session expiry/revocation, the service-side design must meet REQ36-RT-03 without changing the Internal Auth contract. Any ntfy-specific access capability, if needed by the selected Technology, is transport-scoped and cannot authenticate Chat HTTP/history requests or replace the BFE Drive session. Do not forward BFE session credentials or DPoP proofs to ntfy. Only the backend service identity may publish; clients cannot publish or select arbitrary recipients/topics. The concrete ntfy access mechanism is a Technology-stage decision and must not weaken, bypass, or require a change to the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth contract; topic secrecy alone is not authorization.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Regression checks prove that valid DPoP-bound BFE sessions still authenticate protected Chat HTTP requests through the existing Internal Auth UDS integration; Bearer-only, missing/invalid/replayed/misbound proofs and invalid sessions fail closed without Chat side effects. A ntfy topic or transport capability alone cannot authorize protected HTTP/history access. Request captures and logs contain no session credential, DPoP proof, or ntfy access capability in URLs or log fields.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Authoritative session expiry/revocation, logout as observed by the existing session-validation boundary, membership removal, or membership-epoch change must block new ntfy publication to the revoked recipient/epoch. Already-active ntfy access for that session/epoch must be invalidated and protected event delivery must cease within the proposed service-side revocation bound. Rejoining creates a new membership epoch and distinct topic; an old topic or transport capability cannot authorize the new epoch. The service-side design must demonstrate this bound without changing the BFE Drive Internal Auth API or assuming a new Drive callback. If the bound cannot be achieved with the existing integration and selected ntfy configuration, record the exact feasibility gap as blocking evidence; do not weaken authorization or silently change the bound.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Service-level tests or reproducible verification demonstrate that new publication is denied after authoritative session/membership revocation and active access is invalidated within the approved bound; old epoch access fails after rejoin. The evidence identifies the actual revocation signal/check mechanism and distinguishes events accepted before revocation from protected delivery after the bound.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The service emits a versioned wake-up notification whose application body contains an opaque random wakeToken and version only; the token contains no conversation, message, account, or document identifier. The signal is a best-effort invalidation hint, not message state, an ordered cursor, or proof of authorization. Service correctness must not depend on ntfy ordering, cache retention, replay limits, or guaranteed delivery. Durable message ordering and catch-up remain governed by the existing authorized HTTP history API and PostgreSQL-backed conversation ordinal; every history request continues to enforce the caller's current session, membership, and visibility interval. Consumer-specific scheduling, lifecycle, and deduplication behavior is outside this service-only requirements revision.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Service-level checks verify the exact notification envelope, that duplicate/delayed/reordered/lost notifications cannot alter durable message state or ordering, and that the existing history endpoint remains the source of ordered, membership-filtered catch-up. No acceptance criterion depends on unverified behavior in an external client repository.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The complete application-supplied ntfy publish request is allowlisted. The application message body contains exactly integer version and opaque random wakeToken. No application-supplied title, tags, priority, click URL, actions, attachment, sender identity, message text, document ID/title/content, account/conversation/message identifiers, access credential, or other application metadata is permitted. The ntfy topic is opaque and unpredictable and encodes none of those values. ntfy-generated transport fields are not application payload and must not be treated as authoritative. Document ID and title may remain in authorized backend message history and internal backend events where required by the existing message contract, but never in ntfy payload or metadata. Chat membership does not grant BFE Drive document access.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Capture the full publish request and verify the body has only version and wakeToken, the topic is opaque, no application-set metadata is present, and no protected data or credentials appear in ntfy requests or application logs. Verify authorized history still retains required document ID/title and Drive independently denies unauthorized document access.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Notification publication is best-effort and occurs only after durable message commit. A successful message commit remains successful if ntfy publication fails. The service records each notification attempt outcome. An ambiguous/UNKNOWN publish outcome is not automatically retried unless the selected Technology provides evidence that retry is safe; consumed attempts are not blindly replayed. Notification loss must never alter committed message state, bypass authorization, or emit protected payload. Recovery of message history continues through the existing authorized history API; this service requirement does not impose client scheduling or background-delivery guarantees.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Inject definite and ambiguous publication failures after commit. Verify the message remains persisted and readable through the existing authorized history API, the attempt outcome is recorded, no unsafe replay or duplicate durable message occurs, and notification failure does not change authorization or message state.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Every protected history/read request independently validates the current BFE session through the existing Internal Auth/DPoP mechanism and current conversation membership/visibility interval. A notification, ntfy topic, or transport capability never authorizes history access. Multi-device synchronization remains based on the existing backend history and per-account read-state semantics. The transport replacement must not change the established HTTP authentication scheme, route contract, error behavior, or authorization ownership.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: A revoked session cannot read history even if it possesses an old ntfy message or transport capability. Regression checks confirm the existing DPoP-only HTTP authentication and membership-filtered history behavior remain intact.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Chat membership, ntfy topic access, and notification receipt never grant BFE Drive document rights. Document open/download remains independently authorized by BFE Drive. The service continues to preserve document ID/title in authorized backend history where required by the existing message contract; neither ntfy payload nor metadata may expose them. This revision does not add or alter any external subscriber or administrative UI behavior.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Service-level checks show that ntfy payload/metadata contains no document identifier, title, or content, while authorized history preserves the existing document metadata contract. No Chat or ntfy access grants BFE Drive document permissions.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: This proposal authorizes no implementation, dependency change, production configuration change, database migration, merge to the effective baseline, or deployment. Before implementation approval, inventory Centrifuge call sites, dependencies, configuration, publication and revocation behavior within bogachenko/bfe-chat-service only. Define service-side observability, rollout, rollback, and the no-mixed-transport invariant within this repository's scope. Do not inspect or modify BFE Drive, client applications, other repositories, or external infrastructure as part of this revision. Do not claim end-to-end client migration as complete under this service-only scope.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: This requirements-only PR changes no runtime source, dependencies, database, or production configuration. A later implementation gate contains an evidence-backed inventory of service-local Centrifuge usage and tests proving preservation of the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth/DPoP integration and Chat HTTP contract. No external repository or infrastructure is changed by this task.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: This change is confined to the service-side realtime transport contract. It must preserve the existing BFE Drive Internal Auth integration and approved Chat HTTP authentication contract, and must not require a change to BFE Drive's session API, DPoP semantics, or any external client implementation within this requirements revision. Any ntfy-specific subscription access is separate from HTTP session authentication and cannot be accepted as proof for Chat API or history access. Consumer-specific browser/OS matrices, background execution, and external-client rollout are not acceptance criteria for this service-only revision.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: The approved requirements explicitly preserve the existing Internal Auth/DPoP behavior and isolate ntfy access from HTTP/history authorization. Scope review confirms that no other repository, client application, or external infrastructure is required to satisfy this revision's acceptance criteria.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.INVARIANT: Only committed backend state and current backend authorization determine message visibility and access.
The sender is never an ntfy recipient for their own message.
The only application-supplied ntfy body fields are version and opaque wakeToken; no protected content, identifiers, credentials, or custom metadata are supplied.
A revoked session or membership epoch cannot authorize delivery or history access after the approved revocation bound; a rejoined membership uses a new epoch and topic.
ntfy publication failure cannot invalidate or remove a committed backend message.
Notification delivery is best-effort; durable message history and the existing authorized history API remain authoritative and do not depend on notification delivery.

The existing BFE Drive Internal Auth/DPoP session-validation contract and DPoP-only Chat HTTP authentication remain effective; ntfy access never authenticates HTTP/history requests or grants document rights.
This revision is confined to bogachenko/bfe-chat-service and does not authorize changes to BFE Drive, client applications, other repositories, or external infrastructure.

BUSINESS_PROCESS.STEP: An authenticated caller submits a message through the existing Chat HTTP API.
The service validates the BFE session using the existing Internal Auth/DPoP contract, validates current membership and visibility, and durably commits the message.
The service selects currently authorized recipients other than the sender and checks their current membership epochs.
The service publishes a minimal opaque wake-up signal to the recipient's protected epoch topic only after durable commit; publication outcome is recorded.
The signal does not contain message data and does not grant authorization; ordered catch-up remains available only through the existing independently authorized history API.

On session or membership revocation, the service denies new protected publication and invalidates old-epoch ntfy access within the approved service-side bound, without changing the BFE Drive Internal Auth contract.
